clue.text: Bob is brusque and heartlessly cunning

parts.note: brusque means curt, short in manner

indicators.note: heartlessly says the central letter of the word for cunning is cut out

parts.note: cunning means sly

explanation.surface: Someone is described as abrupt and, without compassion, crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is a verb here: to bob is to make a quick bow or dip of the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to dip briefly in respect, which is exactly a small curtsy.

clue.text: Composer's heart's bad when climbing

parts.note: the heart of something is its core

indicators.note: when climbing says the word for bad reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: bad means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: A composer's heart condition worsens as he goes up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concerti grossi.

clue.text: Boulder-strewn and unstable

explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means full of stones and, figuratively, shaky and insecure.

clue.text: Carol spilled the beans, all alone

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
let on means revealed a secret

explanation.surface: A girl named Carol gave away the secret and now has no friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a person or thing on its own, one without a partner.

clue.text: A bobby is put in dock for drink

indicators.note: is put in says the police officer goes inside the word for dock

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, to lop
a bobby is British slang for a police officer, a cop

explanation.surface: A policeman is sent to the dock in court, all over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like the court's dock, but it is the verb meaning to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet fizzy drink containing alcohol, a ready-mixed bottled beverage.

clue.text: Pair prepared bed for fruit tree

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A couple got a garden bed ready for an orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a tree bearing small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Budget for lots and lots

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot
a heap means lots, a great many

explanation.surface: A spending plan allows for a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budget' is an adjective here, as in a budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget item is low-priced, inexpensive, and so is cheap.

clue.text: Quiet citizen becomes chief executive

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a resident is an inhabitant or citizen of a place

explanation.surface: A modest member of the public rises to the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or company, its top executive.

clue.text: Snooker player to mess about

definitions.meaning: in snooker to pot is to sink a ball, so a player who does so

explanation.definitionFit: A potter pots balls at snooker, and to potter is to busy oneself aimlessly.

clue.text: Girl coming out upset teacher? Rubbish!

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a girl coming out into society

indicators.note: upset says the word for teacher is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A society girl's debut upsets a teacher, who shouts in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste and wreckage, the remains of something, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Doctor ran to cure storyteller

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician hurried to heal a patient who loved telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, someone who entertains with stories.

clue.text: Regular time for fixture

parts.note: regular means even, steady

explanation.surface: A sports schedule sets a usual time for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixture is a scheduled sporting occasion, such as a match on a set date.

clue.text: Staunch Labour leader has sovereign beheaded

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Labour
beheaded says the word for sovereign loses its first letter

parts.note: sovereign as an adjective means royal, kingly

explanation.surface: A dedicated Labour Party chief has a monarch executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means faithful and steadfast in support, the same as being true to a cause.

clue.text: Hear about gym that's accessible

indicators.note: about says the word for hear goes round the gym lesson

parts.note: to hear a signal or a guest is to receive it
PT, physical training, is the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: Someone is told about a fitness centre that is easy to get into.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accessible to ideas means being open and willing to take them in.

clue.text: Energy breaks items up

indicators.note: breaks says the letters of the following words are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A burst of power smashes some objects to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is driving force or momentum, the energy behind movement.

clue.text: Penny survived, holding soldier tight

indicators.note: holding says the word for survived contains the soldier

parts.note: lasted means survived, endured
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: Penny pulled through, gripping the soldier closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, not firmly held; RE (Royal Engineers) is a crossword convention for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is British slang for very drunk, as is tight.

clue.text: Word of advice for each benefactor

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint or piece of advice
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: A donor offers a suggestion to each recipient.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little loose: a tipper gives money, so is a small-scale giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper hands over a gratuity, so is a kind of giver to the person served.

clue.text: Reporters joke about new enlistment programme

parts.note: the press is reporters collectively

indicators.note: about says the word for joke goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Journalists make fun of a new recruiting drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang forcibly recruited men into the navy, a crude form of enlistment.

clue.text: Jazz fan shot — found in the garden

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a nip is a small shot of spirits

explanation.surface: A jazz lover is shot dead and discovered among the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a plant of the mint family grown in gardens and loved by cats.

clue.text: Frightened to make amends, when out of jail

indicators.note: when out of says the word for amends is outside the jail word

parts.note: to pay for something is to make amends for it
nick is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: Released prisoners seek to make up for their crimes, nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of jail' suggests release from prison, but here it places the amends word around the prison word.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicky means overcome with sudden fear, frightened.

clue.text: Doubter is poisoned having consumed cocaine

indicators.note: having consumed says the word for poisoned takes the drug inside it

parts.note: septic means infected, poisoned by bacteria
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A doubting person falls ill after taking cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic questions accepted beliefs, a person inclined to disbelieve.

clue.text: Space traveller posed on vessel

indicators.note: on says the posing word rests on top of the vessel in this down clue

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed gives sat
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An astronaut sat for a photo on top of a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, which travels through space in its orbit.

clue.text: Sugar producer keeps longing for spice

indicators.note: keeps says the sugar plant holds the longing word inside

parts.note: sugar cane produces sugar
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A sugar grower keeps craving spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a spice.

clue.text: Grub for fellow the Parisian supports

indicators.note: supports says the French article is placed below the fellow in this down clue

parts.note: a gent is a fellow, a man
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Food for a man is backed by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food, but it is a maggot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle is an angler's name for a maggot, the larva of a fly.

clue.text: Ten items scattered round a bistro

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters are placed around the letter given by a
scattered says the letters of these two words are strewn and reassembled

explanation.surface: Ten objects lie strewn around a small restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café selling drinks, much like a bistro.

clue.text: Public official can overlook alternative

indicators.note: overlook says the word for can sits above the alternative in this down clue

parts.note: may means can, is allowed to
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A civil servant can ignore another option.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a town council, a civic official.

clue.text: Waif to settle outside Reading

indicators.note: outside says the word for settle goes around the letter from reading

parts.note: to stay is to settle somewhere, to remain
reading is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: An orphan is to make a home on the outskirts of the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town, but it is the R of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is a homeless person or animal, as is a waif.

clue.text: Money for a little myrrh in Oman

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a small amount of incense in an Arabian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for money, cash.

clue.text: Wait! That's soiled!

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means smeared with tar, so dirtied

explanation.definitionFit: Tarry is both an old verb for lingering and an adjective for something covered in tar.

clue.text: People after motor that's pink

indicators.note: after says the word for people comes behind the vehicle

parts.note: a motor is a car
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: A crowd follows a pink-painted car.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink is a garden flower of the carnation family, so the bloom is one.

clue.text: See about the German student aging

indicators.note: about says the word for see goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and see (bishop's diocese) in England
der is German for the
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Look at the old German student getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the noun, a bishop's diocese, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes someone advanced in years, growing old.

clue.text: Pass over ravaged region

indicators.note: ravaged means wrecked, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone neglects an area that has been laid waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over something is to overlook it, to disregard it.
